questions.question: Which of the following can be represented as a functional unit of nature?
questions.solution:
An Ecosystem is the functional unit of nature where living organisms interact among themselves and with the surrounding physical environment.
  • It includes Biotic (living) components like plants and animals, and Abiotic (non-living) components like air, water, and soil.
  • Ecosystems can vary in size from a small pond to a vast forest or the entire biosphere.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
questions.option_1: Fats and oils are oxidised, they become rancid.
questions.option_2: Fats and oils get reduced over time and smell bad.
questions.option_3: Antioxidants are added to foods containing fats and oil to prevent oxidation.
questions.option_4: Chips manufacturers usually flush bags of chips with Nitrogen to prevent the chips from getting ranicid.
questions.solution:
The incorrect statement is that fats and oils get 'reduced'; in reality, fats and oils are oxidised to become rancid.
  • Rancidity occurs when the double bonds of an unsaturated fatty acid react with oxygen.
  • This chemical change results in an unpleasant smell and taste.
  • Manufacturers use Nitrogen (an inert gas) to flush bags of chips because it displaces oxygen, preventing oxidation.

questions.question: Which of the following is an inactivated (killed) polio vaccine developed in 1952?
questions.solution:
The Salk vaccine, developed by Jonas Salk in 1952, is an Inactivated Poliovirus Vaccine (IPV).
  • It consists of killed poliovirus strains of all three poliovirus types.
  • Note: The Sabin vaccine is the Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV), which uses a weakened (attenuated) live virus.

questions.question: Which organisms are classified as Aves?
questions.solution:
Birds are classified under the class Aves.
  • Key characteristics of Aves include the presence of feathers, a beak, and forelimbs modified into wings.
  • They are homeothermic (warm-blooded) and have a four-chambered heart.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-perishable food?
questions.solution:
Pulses are considered non-perishable (or stable) foods because they have a low moisture content.
  • Non-perishable foods can be stored for a long period (months or years) at room temperature without spoiling.
  • Meat, milk, and curd are perishable because they have high water and nutrient content, which allows for rapid microbial growth.

questions.question: What do we mean by Allen’s rule?
questions.option_1: Mammals from colder climates generally have shorter ears and limbs to minimise heat loss.
questions.option_2: Desert lizards lack the physiological ability that mammals have to deal with the high temperatures of their habitat.
questions.option_3: Some plants have no leaves – they are reduced to spines – and the photosynthetic function is taken over by the flattened stems.
questions.option_4: The body compensates low oxygen availability by increasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing the breathing rate.
questions.solution:
Allen’s rule states that mammals from colder climates generally have shorter ears and limbs.
  • This is an evolutionary adaptation to minimise heat loss by reducing the surface-area-to-volume ratio.
  • Conversely, animals in hot climates often have larger extremities (like the large ears of an elephant) to help dissipate body heat.

questions.question: The organisms that do not have a defined nucleus or organelles are classified in to _______ Kingdom.
questions.solution:
Organisms that lack a defined nucleus or membrane-bound organelles are classified in the Kingdom Monera.
  • This kingdom primarily consists of Prokaryotes, such as bacteria and cyanobacteria (blue-green algae).
  • Their genetic material is located in an irregularly shaped region called the nucleoid.

questions.question: The growth form of a plant, comprising its size, shape and orientation is known as:
questions.solution:
The Habit of a plant refers to its growth form, including its size, shape, orientation, and general appearance.
  • Common plant habits include herbs, shrubs, trees, and climbers.
  • It is distinct from 'habitat,' which refers to the specific environment where the plant naturally lives.

questions.question: What kind of phyllotaxy was examined in the Guava plant?
questions.solution:
The Guava plant (Psidium guajava) exhibits Opposite phyllotaxy.
  • Phyllotaxy is the pattern of arrangement of leaves on the stem or branch.
  • In opposite phyllotaxy, a pair of leaves arise at each node and lie opposite to each other (e.g., Guava, Calotropis).
  • Note: In Alternate phyllotaxy, a single leaf arises at each node in an alternate manner (e.g., Hibiscus, Mustard).

questions.question: Which of the following plants is used to cure cold and cough?
questions.solution:
Tulsi (Holy Basil) is widely used in traditional medicine to cure cold and cough.
  • It contains bioactive compounds like eugenol that possess anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties.
  • It is a key ingredient in many herbal teas and cough syrups.

questions.question: Name a common electrolyte disorder that occurs when the amount of sodium in your blood becomes abnormally low.
questions.solution:
Hyponatremia is an electrolyte disorder that occurs when sodium levels in the blood are abnormally low.
  • Sodium is crucial for maintaining fluid balance and supporting nerve and muscle function.
  • Symptoms can include nausea, headache, confusion, and fatigue.
  • Note: Hypernatremia refers to high sodium, while Hypokalemia refers to low potassium.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of a flower?
questions.solution:
Spines are not a component of a flower; they are modified leaves or stems used for protection or to reduce water loss.
  • A typical flower consists of four whorls: Calyx (sepals), Corolla (petals), Androecium (male part/stamens), and Gynoecium (female part/pistil).

questions.question: Which branch of ecology deals with the characteristics of ancient environment and their relationship with ancient plants and animals?
questions.solution:
Paleoecology is the branch of ecology that studies ancient environments and their relationships with ancient plants and animals.
  • It relies on fossil records, pollen analysis, and geochemical data to reconstruct past ecosystems.
  • Note: Mycology is the study of fungi, and Ichthyology is the study of fish.

questions.question: Who published Systema Naturae in 1735 classifying the three kingdoms of nature and outlining the sexual system for the classification of plants?
questions.solution:
Carolus Linnaeus published Systema Naturae in 1735.
  • He is known as the Father of Taxonomy.
  • He introduced the Binomial Nomenclature system (the two-part scientific naming of species).
  • He outlined the sexual system of classification based on the number and arrangement of reproductive organs in plants.

questions.question: Which of the following options indicates the size of PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms)?
questions.solution:
PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms), also known as Mycoplasma, are about 0.1 µm in size.
  • They are the smallest known living cells.
  • Unlike other bacteria, they lack a cell wall, which makes them naturally resistant to many common antibiotics like penicillin.

questions.question: Which of the following options is associated with the class of cold-blooded animals?
questions.solution:
A Chameleon belongs to the class Reptilia, which are cold-blooded (poikilothermic) animals.
  • Cold-blooded animals cannot regulate their internal body temperature and rely on external heat sources.
  • The other options—Macropus (Kangaroo), Psittacula (Parrot), and Pavo (Peacock)—are all warm-blooded (mammals or birds).

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics is NOT of Aves?
questions.option_2: They give birth to live young ones with some exceptions those lay eggs.
questions.solution:
The statement that Aves 'give birth to live young ones' is incorrect.
  • All birds are oviparous, meaning they lay eggs.
  • They have a four-chambered heart, are warm-blooded, and breathe through lungs assisted by air sacs.

questions.question: Digestion of food is an important function of the animal body. In animals like lions, cows, humans, etc., the process involves use of various organs starting from the mouth and ending with the anus. The longest part of this canal is known as the ________.
questions.solution:
The small intestine is the longest part of the alimentary canal (digestive tract).
  • Despite being called 'small' due to its diameter, it is roughly 6 to 7 meters long in humans.
  • It is the primary site for the complete digestion of food and the absorption of nutrients.

questions.question: How many chambers are there in the heart of fishes?
questions.solution:
The heart of a fish has 2 chambers.
  • It consists of one atrium and one ventricle.
  • Fishes exhibit single circulation, where blood passes through the heart only once during a complete circuit of the body.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
questions.option_2: Mitochondria: Power house of the cell
questions.solution:
The pair 'Nucleus: Lipid metabolism' is incorrectly matched.
  • The Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) is the primary site for lipid metabolism.
  • The Nucleus contains the cell's genetic material and controls cellular activities through gene expression.

questions.question: What is the reason for the similar size of the vascular bundle in monocot leaves?
questions.solution:
In monocot leaves, the vascular bundles are of similar size because of Parallel venation.
  • In monocots, veins run parallel to each other from the base to the tip of the leaf.
  • This arrangement results in vascular bundles of almost uniform size (except for the main vein) arranged in a linear fashion.

questions.question: Microbes like Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are used for:
questions.solution:
Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas, and Nitrobacter are essential microbes for the Nitrogen cycle.
  • Rhizobium: Fixes atmospheric nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes.
  • Nitrosomonas: Converts ammonia into nitrites.
  • Nitrobacter: Converts nitrites into nitrates.

questions.question: What are the five Fs of indirect transmission?
questions.option_1: Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fruit
questions.option_2: Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fluid
questions.option_3: Fruit, fingers, flu, food and fluid
questions.option_4: Flies, fingers, friends, food and fruit
questions.solution:
The five Fs of indirect disease transmission are: Flies, Fingers, Fomites, Food, and Fluid.
  • Fomites are inanimate objects (like doorknobs or towels) that can carry infection.
  • These pathways demonstrate how pathogens move from an infected host to a new susceptible host.

questions.question: Which set of diseases are caused by bacteria?
questions.solution:
Typhoid, Cholera, and Tuberculosis are all caused by bacteria.
  • Typhoid: Salmonella typhi.
  • Cholera: Vibrio cholerae.
  • Tuberculosis: Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
  • Note: Influenza and Dengue are viral, while Malaria is caused by a protozoan (Plasmodium).

questions.question: Which is a serious contagious bacterial infection that usually affects the mucous membranes of the nose and throat?
questions.solution:
Diphtheria is a serious contagious bacterial infection caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
  • It primarily affects the mucous membranes of the nose and throat.
  • A hallmark sign is a thick, gray coating (pseudomembrane) that builds up in the throat, which can cause breathing difficulties.
